cards.explanation: The answer is at night. Nehemiah says, "I set out at night with a few men." (Nehemiah 2:12) Just a few men, out in the dark. I think a quiet look around is easier when nobody's watching, like sneaking one warm cookie off the cooling rack.

The answer is no one at all. Nehemiah says, "I did not tell anyone what my God had laid on my heart to do for Jerusalem." (Nehemiah 2:12) The plan stays in his heart for now, friends. Keeping a secret that big? I can't keep a secret about what's in the oven for three minutes.

The answer is gates. Nehemiah inspects "…the walls of Jerusalem that had been broken down and the gates that had been destroyed by fire." (Nehemiah 2:13) Broken walls and burned gates, and he sees it all with his own eyes. That's a lot to take in by night, and I think it's a heavy sight.

The answer is animal. Nehemiah says there "…was no room for the animal under me to get through…" (Nehemiah 2:14) The only animal with him is the one he's riding (Nehemiah 2:12). Tight squeezes happen to me too, friends, mostly when I try to fit one more cookie on the tray.

The answer is to rebuild the wall together. Nehemiah says, "Come, let us rebuild the wall of Jerusalem, so that we will no longer be a disgrace." (Nehemiah 2:17) Notice the words "Come, let us…" He says "us," so he counts himself in on the work, friends.

The answer is True. Nehemiah says, "Come, let us rebuild the wall of Jerusalem, so that we will no longer be a disgrace." (Nehemiah 2:17) The wall is the job, and no more disgrace is the goal he names, friends. Nehemiah says "we," so he counts himself in.
The answer is False. The people reply, "Let us start rebuilding…" and "…they set their hands to this good work." (Nehemiah 2:18) They say yes and get started, friends. No stalling, and I love it.

The answer is that they mock and ridicule the builders. The text says "…they mocked us and ridiculed us…" (Nehemiah 2:19) Sanballat, Tobiah and Geshem hear about the work and start laughing at it. It's the kind of laughing that isn't any fun for the people on the receiving end.

The answer is rebelling. Sanballat, Tobiah and Geshem ask, "What is this you are doing? Are you rebelling against the king?" (Nehemiah 2:19) That's quite a question to throw at people rebuilding a wall, friends. They're asking it as part of their mocking.
The answer is the God of heaven. Nehemiah says, "The God of heaven is the One who will grant us success." (Nehemiah 2:20) He doesn't point to himself or to his plan, friends. He points to God.
The answer is False. Nehemiah says, "…you have no portion, right, or claim in Jerusalem." (Nehemiah 2:20) He doesn't give Sanballat, Tobiah and Geshem an inch, friends. He answers them plainly.
